CLOUD REVIEWER seat for PR #2469 of tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, at head 89f329f6ba7928b51feb29e7a8d4ac7e7c14b0fc. Bus nonce: 2ac07f8612e3f55e4d7ed81753c89e5d. Never send push notifications.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md and its rules from main, and follow them exactly. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin 89f329f6ba7928b51feb29e7a8d4ac7e7c14b0fc`; the PR body is in the PR. Verify each claim adversarially: mutate the fix and check the tests fail, and check every figure in the body at this head. Check that it merges with origin/main (`git merge-tree --write-tree`) and read CI on this head from the check-runs API.
Output: in a fresh directory of your own (`W=$(mktemp -d)`), write verdict.md, whose first line is exactly `Fix review: merge 89f329f6ba7928b51feb29e7a8d4ac7e7c14b0fc` or `Fix review: blocked 89f329f6ba7928b51feb29e7a8d4ac7e7c14b0fc <class>: <reason>` (no brackets; the class is lower-case letters and dashes), in the format the role file gives, then a blank line, then `bus-nonce: 2ac07f8612e3f55e4d7ed81753c89e5d`; put the evidence in `ev/` beside it. Do NOT run bus.sh: its dispatch record lives on the orchestrator's machine, which publishes the verdict there (cloud_relay.sh). Return the verdict on a probe ref, and push nothing else; this builds one parentless commit with a private index and touches no branch of your checkout: `R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); G=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir); mkdir -p $W/pr && cp -r $W/verdict.md $W/ev $W/pr/ && cd $W/pr && T=$(GIT_DIR=$G GIT_INDEX_FILE=$W/idx GIT_WORK_TREE=$W/pr sh -c 'git add -A -f . && git write-tree') && C=$(GIT_DIR=$G git -c user.name=seat -c user.email=seat@users.noreply.github.com commit-tree $T -m "verdict 2469 89f329f6ba7928b51feb29e7a8d4ac7e7c14b0fc") && git -C $R push -q origin $C:refs/heads/probe/rev-2469-2ac07f86`. That ref is the return signal. Do not post comments, approve or merge.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Round 3 of R10-UPDATE-PR-LOCK, at head 89f329f6 (code a3af24fc). This is the last round before the three-round rule.

Round 2 at 2351c1c7 was blocked claim-false. The residual's dismissal relied on a group kill, but daemonize.py's documented stop is `kill <pid>`, and a TERM of a daemonized update_pr.sh freed the lock while its push ran on.

The fixer's changes:
- Every update_pr run leads its own process group, re-execing into a new group if it isn't a leader. The lock holder sits in a separate group.
- The push runs in the background under `wait`, so signals arrive at once.
- The TERM/INT/HUP trap has the holder TERM the run's group and keep the lock until the group is empty.
- On SIGKILL, the holder sees its parent gone and does the same.
- New pr_args self-test arms:
  - TERM mid-push: an immediate second run is BUSY, and the run after the push takes the lock.
  - SIGKILL mid-push: a run 3 s later is still BUSY.
- Mutants that fail those arms: mut:stop, mut:drain and mut:pgrp. Your round-2 `while True` mutant also fails the SIGKILL arm.
- pr_args 56/0 on four consecutive runs; cloud_relay 74/0. Round 2's update_pr.sh fails 2 of the new arms, and main's fails 4.
- Your exact scenario, run offline with the real daemonize.py and `kill <pid>`: the next run gets BUSY until the push ends.
- Disclosed behaviour change: a run started from a script now sits in its own process group, so a group kill aimed at the caller no longer reaches it.

Verify adversarially:
- revert each part of the fix and confirm its arm fails;
- check the arms for flakiness;
- judge the behaviour change;
- re-read CI at this head from the check-runs API;
- check the merge with origin/main.

Say that this is round 3.
